blocks.text: W lekcji 9 mówiłeś, co dzieje się teraz: I am reading. Teraz — co działo się w jakimś momencie przeszłości: «czytałem komiks», «czyściłem botki, kiedy zadzwoniłeś», «wąchała kwiaty, podczas gdy ja mówiłem».

examples.en: I was reading a comic book.
They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.
I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.
She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.
examples.translation: Wąchała kwiaty, podczas gdy ja mówiłem.

blocks.text: Po polsku «czytałem» to i proces, i fakt. Po angielsku proces w przeszłości mówi się osobno: to lekcja 9 przeniesiona w przeszłość — was / were zamiast am / is / are, a -ing na swoim miejscu. I was reading — «właśnie czytałem».

examples.en: I was reading a comic book.
She was using a colouring book.
I was cooking fried rice.
We were eating a spring roll.
They were watching the soap bubbles.

fixes.right: I was reading a comic book.

fixes.wrong: They was doing a jigsaw puzzle.
fixes.right: They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.

drill.why: Z they w przeszłości — were, a -ing już jest.

blocks.text: «Nie» jak zawsze — po was lub were: I wasn't playing, they weren't watching. wasn't to was not, weren't to were not. -ing zostaje.

examples.en: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.
I wasn't writing in the homework diary.
examples.translation: Nie pisałem w zeszycie z zadaniami domowymi.

examples.en: I wasn't watching the robin.

fixes.wrong: I not was playing on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

fixes.wrong: I didn't playing on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

blocks.text: Pytanie — was lub were na początek, jak w lekcjach 2 i 9: Were you playing in the paddling pool? Was he watching the owl? Did nie jest tu potrzebne: Did you playing to błąd.

examples.en: Were you playing in the paddling pool?
Was he jumping on the trampoline?
Were you using the workbook?
Was he watching the owl?

fixes.wrong: Did you playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

fixes.wrong: You were playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

drill.question: Zapytaj, czy wtedy patrzył na sowę. Które zdanie jest poprawne?
drill.explain: Z -ing pytanie zaczyna się od was lub were, nie od did.

blocks.text: Tej formy używa się, żeby narysować tło: co ludzie robili, kiedy zaczęła się historia. I was changing a flat tyre — «zmieniałem przebitą oponę». To nie osobne wydarzenie, tylko coś, co trwało.

examples.en: I was changing a flat tyre.
He was checking the windscreen wiper.
We were cleaning the rear-view mirror.
She was packing the nappy bag.

sections.title: when — coś się stało w trakcie

blocks.text: Jeśli coś się stało w trakcie procesu, proces to was / were + -ing, a zdarzenie — zwykła przeszłość po when: I was cleaning my boots when you called. Telefon był krótki i przerwał czyszczenie.

examples.en: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.
She was packing her ballet flats when I called.
We were looking for an insole when you arrived.
She was drawing a piece of driftwood when I arrived.
examples.translation: Rysowała kawałek drewna wyrzuconego przez morze, kiedy przyszedłem.

fixes.wrong: I cleaned my ankle boots when you were calling.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

fixes.wrong: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you were call.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

blocks.text: while — «podczas gdy», «kiedy (przez cały czas)». Używa się go, gdy dwa procesy trwały jednocześnie, i w obu częściach jest was / were + -ing: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.

examples.en: I was looking up while you were taking a photo.
examples.translation: Patrzyłem w górę, podczas gdy ty robiłeś zdjęcie.

examples.en: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.
examples.translation: Wąchała kwiaty, podczas gdy ja mówiłem.

examples.en: We were giggling while he was telling the story.
I was cutting celery while you were cooking.
examples.translation: Kroiłem seler, podczas gdy ty gotowałeś.

blocks.text: Po polsku i when, i while to często «kiedy». Po angielsku jest różnica. Krótkie zdarzenie, które przerwało proces, — when + zwykła przeszłość: when you called. Długi proces równoległy — while + was / were + -ing.

examples.en: We were watching a wasp when you called.
I was watching a butterfly while you were taking a photo.
examples.translation: Patrzyłem na motyla, podczas gdy ty robiłeś zdjęcie.

examples.en: I was turning around when you called my name.
examples.translation: Odwracałem się, kiedy zawołałeś mnie po imieniu.

fixes.wrong: They was doing a jigsaw puzzle.
fixes.right: They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.

fixes.wrong: I didn't playing on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

fixes.wrong: Did you playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

fixes.wrong: I cleaned my ankle boots when you were calling.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

fixes.wrong: She was sniffing the flowers when I was talking.
fixes.right: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.

blocks.text: Proces w przeszłości — was / were + -ing. Krótkie zdarzenie, które go przerwało, — zwykła przeszłość po when. Did nie łączy się z -ing.
Coś trwało — was / were + -ing, zawsze z kto. «Nie» — wasn't / weren't. Pytanie — Was…? Were…? Przerwało — when + zwykła przeszłość. Jednocześnie — while + was / were + -ing.

examples.en: I was filling a spray bottle.
Were you taking a photo of the woodpecker?
I was looking at a starfish when you called.
I was using a glue stick while you were drawing.
examples.translation: Używałem kleju w sztyfcie, podczas gdy ty rysowałeś.
